questions.question: The constraint $2x_1+x_2\ge4$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) is written as $2x_1+x_2-S_1=4$ with surplus $S_1\ge0$. Why can the surplus alone not provide a starting point with $x_1=x_2=0$?
options: It would need $S_1=4$, which overstates the excess
A surplus may never be positive at a starting point
At $x=0$ it would need $S_1=-4$, breaking $S_1\ge0$
A surplus is only allowed after $x_1$ becomes positive

questions.question: For an equality $\sum_ja_{ij}x_j=b_i$ with $b_i\ge0$, an artificial variable is added as $\sum_ja_{ij}x_j+R_i=b_i$ with $R_i\ge0$. Why is it added with coefficient $+1$?
options: Then $R_i$ measures the excess of the row above $b_i$
Then the row becomes a $\le$ constraint again
Then $R_i$ has a cost of 1 per unit in the LP
Then $R_i=b_i\ge0$ when all other variables are 0

questions.question: An auxiliary problem for artificial variables $R_1,R_2\ge0$ is stated as: maximize $-R_1-R_2$ subject to the rewritten constraints. Which problem has the same optimal solutions?
options: Maximize $R_1+R_2$
Minimize $-R_1-R_2$
Maximize $R_1-R_2$
Minimize $R_1+R_2$

questions.question: An LP has variables $x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$ and four constraints with positive right-hand sides: two $\le$, one $\ge$ and one $=$. Each $\le$ row gets a slack; the $\ge$ row gets a surplus and an artificial; the $=$ row gets an artificial. How many variables does the rewritten problem have?
The equation $2x_1+3x_2=6$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) is written as $2x_1+3x_2+R_1=6$ with artificial $R_1\ge0$. What is $R_1$ at $x_1=1$, $x_2=1$, and what does it say?
options: $R_1=-1$: the original equation is exceeded
$R_1=1$: the original equation is short by 1
$R_1=0$: any point with $x\ge0$ satisfies it
$R_1=6$: the starting value never changes

questions.question: Constraints $x_1+x_2\le8$, $2x_1+x_2\ge5$ and $x_1-x_2=2$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) become $x_1+x_2+s_1=8$, $2x_1+x_2-S_2+R_2=5$, $x_1-x_2+R_3=2$. At the start $x_1=x_2=S_2=0$. Which values do the other variables take?

An equality constraint $x_1+x_2=5$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) needs a variable that can start at 5 when $x_1=x_2=0$. Why is a slack $s\ge0$, as in $x_1+x_2+s=5$, not acceptable here, while an artificial $R$ is?
options: A slack stays in the model and turns $=5$ into $\le5$
A slack would start at $-5$, which breaks $s\ge0$
A slack has a positive cost, an artificial a zero cost
A slack can only be used for $\ge$ constraints

questions.question: Rows $2x_1+3x_2+R_1=6$ and $3x_1-x_2-S_1+R_2=4$ (all variables $\ge0$) come from $2x_1+3x_2=6$ and $3x_1-x_2\ge4$. A solution has $x=(3,0)$, $S_1=5$, $R_1=R_2=0$. What does it say about the original constraints?
options: The $\ge$ row fails, since $S_1=5$ is positive
Both hold; $3x_1-x_2$ exceeds the bound 4 by 5
They hold only once $S_1$ is also driven to 0
Only the equation holds; the other is unclear

questions.question: The constraint $x_1-x_2\ge0$ (with $x_1,x_2\ge0$) must be prepared for a start at $x_1=x_2=0$. Is an artificial variable needed?
options: No: as $-x_1+x_2\le0$ it takes a slack starting at 0
Yes: every $\ge$ constraint needs an artificial variable
Yes: the surplus starts at a negative value at $x=0$
No: the constraint can be dropped, as $x=0$ satisfies it

questions.question: An auxiliary problem for artificial variables $R_1,R_2\ge0$ must drive both to zero. A student proposes to minimize $R_1-R_2$ instead of $R_1+R_2$. Why does this fail?
options: It is unbounded, since $R_1$ can grow without limit
It makes the starting point $R_1=b_1$, $R_2=b_2$ infeasible
It rewards a large $R_2$, so $R_2$ need not reach 0
It works equally well, as both are linear objectives

questions.question: Rows $2x_1+3x_2+R_1=6$ and $3x_1-x_2-S_1+R_2=4$ (all variables $\ge0$) come from $2x_1+3x_2=6$ and $3x_1-x_2\ge4$. With $x=(2,0)$ fixed and $S_1,R_1,R_2$ free to choose, what is the smallest possible $R_1+R_2$?

An LP maximizes $x_1+x_2$ s.t. $2x_1+3x_2=6$, $3x_1-x_2\ge4$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Minimizing $R_1+R_2$ in the rewritten rows reaches $R_1=R_2=0$ at $x=(2,\frac{2}{3})$. What does this point tell us about the original LP?
options: It is feasible, though $(3,0)$ is better, so it is not optimal
It is optimal, since the artificials reached the best value 0
It is infeasible, since the surplus $S_1=\frac{4}{3}$ is positive
It is feasible, and its value $\frac{8}{3}$ bounds the optimum above
